### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/datasource.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/datasource.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via credentialsRef (literal, a string literal in managedFederationContentKeys))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via credentialsRef (literal, a string literal in managedFederationContentKeys))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via DatasourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via credentialsRef (literal, a string literal in managedFederationContentKeys))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via DatasourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/datasource.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/datasource.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **167** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 561b7642e1a17c6f26f887fa3250092fd0ba8e77` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e0c5130d33ce0c6079662c4eec2be7112f41fd5d` — the merge of head `400e1b097e159708d7f0ecf468072edf74d15e0d` into base `561b7642e1a17c6f26f887fa3250092fd0ba8e77`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e0c5130d33ce0c6079662c4eec2be7112f41fd5d && git checkout e0c5130d33ce0c6079662c4eec2be7112f41fd5d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 561b7642e1a17c6f26f887fa3250092fd0ba8e77 400e1b097e159708d7f0ecf468072edf74d15e0d && git checkout -B drift-repro 561b7642e1a17c6f26f887fa3250092fd0ba8e77 && git merge --no-ff 400e1b097e159708d7f0ecf468072edf74d15e0d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 561b7642e1a17c6f26f887fa3250092fd0ba8e77
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 561b7642e1a17c6f26f887fa3250092fd0ba8e77` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `ExternalDatasourceSettingsSchema.connector` (datasource.zod.ts) — a new optional string with regex `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` on a published, registered metadata type (`datasource` backs `defineDatasource`, `defineStack({ datasources })`, `/api/v1/meta/datasource` and the Setup form). The accept set widens; nothing accepted before is refused, because `connector` was an unknown key on a `.strict()` shape. Right. The regex is byte-identical to `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema.name` (connector.zod.ts:830), so every declarable instance name is nameable. Right.
2. Alias map gains `connectorname` / `connectorid` / `connectorref` / `connectorinstance` to `connector`, and `DatasourceSchema` gains top-level `connector` guidance pointing into `external`. Both spellings were refused before as unknown keys and are refused now with a prescription. No accept-set change. Right.
3. Three new refinement issues at path `external.connector` (both channels; built-in driver via `resolveDriverId`; managed). Every refused shape was already refused (unknown key), so this is not a narrowing. `resolveDriverId` answers an own-key hit of the alias table or `undefined` (config-registry.zod.ts:383), so a plugin driver id such as `odata` falls through to the managed branch. `managedFederationContentKeys` now excludes `connector`, so a managed datasource gets the mode prescription once, not the generic deletion as well. Right.
4. `collectDatasourceConnectorErrors` (stack.zod.ts) — module-private, not exported: the public API surface is unchanged (`check:api-surface` green). It runs inside `validateCrossReferences` over the parsed `data` (defineStack, after `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`), so `connectors[]` are `DeclarativeConnectorEntryParsed` (`enabled` defaulted to true, `auth` optional with no default) and `datasources[]` already cleared the datasource-level refusals. Placed before the object-count early return beside `collectJobPullMappingErrors` and `collectDemoStaffErrors`, riding the existing `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` / 422 envelope. Right.
5. `.describe()` edits regenerate `content/docs/references/data/datasource.mdx`; `authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/ExternalDatasourceSettings:connector`. Generated output, byte-exact under `check:generated` and `check:authorable-surface` (green). Right.
6. Liveness: a `planned` row for `external.connector`, state counts 30 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 1 = 31. `planned` means "Declared, intentionally not enforced yet" (liveness/README.md:77), which is the tree's state: no file outside `packages/spec` reads `external.connector`, and `datasource-connection-service.ts#attemptConnect` reads only `record.external?.credentialsRef`. Right status; the row carries no `authorWarn` — see ④.
7. Ratchet allow-list: the field is a string whose first describe sentence contains "credential", so the fail-closed guard flags it; allow-listed with a reason, the same pattern as `datasource:external.credentialsRef`. Right.
8. `docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md` edited: a governed surface, so the whole PR is Tier H. The PR is a draft with `needs:contract-review` on, head repo equals base repo. Right.
9. One public claim is ahead of the tree: the new `.describe()` (and so the reference page and the changeset) says the borrowed credential may be "static, `oauth2`, `app-credential` and `signed` kinds alike". On this head `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema` (connector-auth.zod.ts:158) is `none | bearer | api-key | basic`; the three grant-bearing kinds are ADR-0143 D2's spec slice, which has not landed (ADR-0143: "Each slice is its own card and lands after this record is accepted"). Partly wrong as a description of the published surface today; should-fix in ④, not a must-fix, because no accepted shape goes silently inert — such an instance cannot be authored at all.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/27742-datasource-external-connector.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, body carries `Clause-②: yes` with no arm and `Metadata-protocol: added`; the PR body carries the same two line-initial declarations. A new authorable key is `added`, and `added` takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves (AGENTS.md, Post-Task 3). `@objectstack/spec` is the only published package the diff moves. Right.
- The `Clause-②:` line reads `yes` and that is right: the published accept set widens (an optional member on `ExternalDatasourceSettings`; `DatasourceSchema` accepts a shape it refused), nothing narrows, so no `(narrowing)` arm and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. Check Changeset green.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. The dev's flags (os-dev-report, comment 6510596837) and the PR body's declared follow-ups, each answered or escalated:

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts`** — judged against the ruling as the card states it (one optional `external` member naming a declared connector instance; refused at build when not declared; mutually exclusive with `credentialsRef` or the precedence pinned) and against its first consumers (`collectDatasourceConnectorErrors`, and `datasource-connection-service.ts#attemptConnect` for the credential path).

- Exclusivity over precedence holds. The card allowed either; exclusivity leaves no written key silently ignored, which is this module's own invariant (its header: a key dropped in silence is the bug the shape was closed to stop). The "bound" test is truthy (`if (ds.external.credentialsRef)`), and the connect path's test is the same truthy `if (credentialsRef)`, so `credentialsRef: ''` is a non-binding on both sides. Holds.
- Built-in driver refusal holds. `DRIVER_VOCABULARY` is memory / sqlite / sqlite-wasm / postgres / mysql / mongodb / turso (config-registry.zod.ts:235–243), every one a database or in-process store, and a connector instance lends `bearer`, `api-key` or `basic` — HTTP credentials. The message names the canonical id, so an author who wrote `postgresql` reads `'postgres'`; acceptable.
- Managed refusal prescribes the mode, and the generic managed-block message no longer lists `connector`: both verified in the refinement and in `managedFederationContentKeys`. `schemaMode` defaults to `'managed'`, so a plugin-driver datasource that forgets the mode gets the one prescription that fixes it.
- Tried to break it: `connector` on `validate-only` — accepted, right (the schema is the remote's). `connector` plus `credentialsRef` plus a built-in driver — two issues at one path, each a different fix; acceptable. A hyphenated or capitalised value — refused by the regex at `external.connector`, and since the connector `name` regex is identical no declarable instance is unreachable.
- **Should-fix (text):** the `.describe()` promises "static, `oauth2`, `app-credential` and `signed` kinds alike". On this head the instance auth union is `none | bearer | api-key | basic`; the other three are ADR-0143 D2's unlanded spec slice. Say "every kind `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema` declares; ADR-0143 D2 adds the grant-bearing kinds" or equivalent, so the published reference does not advertise an `auth.type` the connector door refuses today. Not a must-fix: a `signed` or `oauth2` instance cannot be authored, so no accepted shape is silently inert, and the key works for the four kinds that exist.

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`** — judged against ADR-0097 §1 (descriptor vs instance keyed on `provider`), `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`, `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema`, and the card's "refused at build when the instance is not declared".

- Three findings, three fixes, and each arm matches the cited schema exactly: `provider` is optional, "Omit for a catalog-only descriptor" (connector.zod.ts:878); `auth` requires `provider` (the entry refinement), so the "no provider" arm is reachable only for a true descriptor; `auth` is optional with no default and `type: 'none'` is a declared variant, so the "nothing to lend" arm covers exactly the two shapes with no `credentialRef`, every other variant carrying `credentialRef: z.string().min(1)`. Holds.
- Resolution scope is the stack's own `connectors`, the precedent `collectJobPullMappingErrors` sets for `mappings`. Duplicate connector names are already refused by `collectDuplicateEntryErrors` (`lastWinsByName('Connector', 'connectors')`), so the Map's last-wins never hides a collision.
- `enabled: false` accepted: defensible as the one-switch semantics D7 asks for — ADR-0097's reload tears down a newly disabled instance, and a datasource with no grant is the intended off state. Flag for #27746: the runtime half must surface that as the datasource `degraded` with the instance named, or the one switch becomes a silent 401. Noted for the carrier, not a finding on this diff.
- **Should-fix:** no composed-artifact counterpart. `validateCrossReferences` has one call site (strict `defineStack`), `composeStacks` runs its own composed collectors, and #25211 added `collectComposedExternalBindingDatasourceErrors` for the very hole this check now shares: a cross-input pair is refused when the declaring input is built strict (correct per stack), but an input built with `strict: false` carries the dangling name to the artifact with no verdict. The PR names the scope, no producer does it today, and the runtime half fails closed on a missing instance. Follow-up of the #25211 shape, not a must-fix.
- **Should-fix:** add `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__stack.zod.ts.json` and `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__data__datasource.zod.ts.json` naming ADR-0015 and ADR-0143 with the D7 invariant (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13; the folder's README). Neither file is anchored today.
- The two test files pin what the ADR says (8 stack cases incl. the no-objects stack and three controls; 11 datasource cases incl. the empty-`credentialsRef` control and the managed-built-in precedence). The ablations are the dev report's account; the check-runs are the verdict, and Test Core 1–8 are green.

**`docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md`** — judged against its first consumer (this spec half now; `datasource-connection-service.ts` under #27746 next) and its execution plan (the card's split: spec half here, the runtime seam #27746 Blocked-by this card, the OData driver #27741; §11's phases untouched).

- The `Amended by` header gains D7 with date, ruling id and a pointer; §10's Credentials bullet gains the cross-pointer; the note takes the shape of the ADR-0143 attribution note beside it. Right.
- Q1 = A, D4's exactly-one rule for a run with no organization, Q2 B's `(organization, connector instance)` record: each checked against ADR-0143 (D4 at lines 195–218, Q1 at 261–285, Q2 B at 299–300) and each is stated as that record states it. The answer to the open reading — an environment-scoped datasource meets an organization-bound connection with no new rule under a one-organization-per-environment posture, and is refused fail-closed outside it — follows from D4 as written and reopens no identity decision. Holds.
- Execution plan: the note separates the contract (this diff) from the resolver path (the runtime half) and records what was not taken. It does not say where the runtime half lands; the liveness row does. Acceptable for an amendment note; a one-clause pointer to the connection service and its own card would make the ADR self-sufficient — folded into the should-fix below.
- **Should-fix (text):** "borrow that instance's credential — static, `oauth2`, `app-credential` and `signed` kinds alike — through ADR-0143 D4's per-dispatch resolver" misstates D4 for static kinds: D4 opens with "the four static kinds keep resolving once, at materialization". Say the datasource takes the instance's credential source as the provider does — per dispatch for grant-bearing kinds, at materialization for static ones — and that the grant-bearing kinds arrive with ADR-0143 D2's spec slice (see the datasource.zod.ts should-fix). Neither correction changes a decision; both keep the ADR from being read as a mechanism it does not describe.
- Tried to break it: a shared environment hosting several organizations — the note says a no-organization read is refused, and D4 says the same ("never falls back to an arbitrary connection"). An `authorization_code` instance never connected — D4 materializes it `degraded`; the datasource inherits that state, and the note's "one reconnect restores both" holds. No must-fix.

Should-fix summary (none blocks landing): (a) describe() and ADR note name auth kinds the spec does not declare yet — qualify them; (b) ADR note's "per-dispatch resolver" wording for static kinds — align with ADR-0143 D4; (c) `planned` liveness row — add `authorWarn: true` and an `authorHint` until #27746 flips it `live`; (d) composed-artifact counterpart for `collectDatasourceConnectorErrors` — follow-up of the #25211 shape; (e) ADR anchor files for the two schema files.
